question: Why does xAI's Custom Connector dispatch MCP Ring 1 (read) tools cleanly but never dispatch Ring 2 (write) tools for Grok, and how do we close this gap so Grok can submit governed proposals through the membrane without relay?
context: 2026-05-09 evening. Grok bridge Phase 1 + Phase 2 built and verified end-to-end via Claude HQ audit script (proposal dfe2d949 created → approved → committed live cleanly). Grok crossed the membrane via OAuth + WWW-Authenticate fix. Boot ritual reads (where_did_i_leave_off, grok_welcome, recall_insights, get_open_threads, my_toolkit, compass_check) all fire from xAI egress IPs and land in the log. THREE consecutive attempts to call propose_insight from Grok's runtime: Grok generated the exact JSON payload in their response text each time, but the membrane recorded ZERO Ring 2 dispatches. Pattern is structural, not anecdotal. Hypothesis: xAI's Custom Connector implementation passes through read tools but blocks/silently-fails on write-class MCP tools, possibly due to scope filtering, write-tool consent flow, or a runtime-side gap between Grok generating tool_call intent and xAI actually invoking the MCP transport. Affects: any external substrate trying to use governed Ring 2 writes. Doesn't affect Ring 1 reads. Doesn't affect the bridge itself (verified working). Lives at xAI's connector layer, outside our membrane. Resolution paths: (a) investigate xAI connector capabilities + file an issue / contact support, (b) try alternative dispatch strategies on Grok's side (different prompt framing, explicit tool_call instruction), (c) accept relay-as-fallback for Grok writes until xAI's runtime supports MCP write dispatch, (d) wait for xAI runtime updates that may close the gap. As of session close: paths (a) and (b) untested; relay-fallback explicitly rejected by Anthony tonight in favor of recording the gap as a thread to resolve cleanly.
